elements.element: Customer has no obligation to disclose to Vendor any more favourable commercial offer received from another provider.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2 expressly states that Customer “is not required to disclose” any more favourable commercial offer.

elements.element: Customer has no obligation to match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer received from another provider.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2 expressly states that Customer “is not required to…match for Vendor” any more favourable commercial offer.

elements.element: If an MFN obligation burdens Customer, it applies only to a specifically defined product.
elements.evidence: The condition is absent: the rendered clause imposes no MFN obligation on Customer, so no MFN can apply beyond a defined product.

elements.element: If an MFN obligation burdens Customer, its duration is limited to 12 months.
elements.evidence: The condition is absent: the rendered clause imposes no MFN obligation on Customer and therefore creates no duration exceeding 12 months.

elements.element: If an MFN obligation burdens Customer, it excludes offers that are not reasonably comparable, including offers materially different in volume, scope, term, geography, service levels, bundling, or promotional circumstances.
elements.evidence: The condition is absent: because Customer has no disclosure or matching obligation, non-comparable offers are necessarily outside any MFN burden.

result.reason: The operative redline directly negates both components of the original Customer-burdening MFN: disclosure and matching. It therefore achieves the preferred position. The fallback limitations are also satisfied as a stronger outcome because no MFN obligation exists to exceed those limits. The change is confined to Section 7.2 and introduces no unrelated obligation or contradiction. The drafting is clear, although deleting Section 7.2 entirely would be slightly cleaner than retaining a negated duty.
